intent: To illustrate the significant disparity in voter registration between white and nonwhite populations in Southern states in 1963, which resulted in political overrepresentation for the white electorate.

requirements.question: Must the video explicitly compare the two registration rates, or is showing unequal bar heights sufficient?
Must the video convey that most Nonwhite adults could not vote, not just their 40% registration rate?
Must the video compare couldn't-vote shares across groups, or is the Nonwhite 60% figure alone sufficient?

units.claim: White voter registration was 74%, compared with 40% for Nonwhite adults.
accept: White voter registration was 74%, versus 40% for Nonwhite adults.
74% of White adults were registered, compared with 40% of Nonwhite adults.
Nonwhite registration stood at 40% while White registration was 74%.
units.evidence: Both registered segments must be visible/labeled at 74% for White and 40% for Nonwhite, ideally side by side.

units.claim: Among Nonwhite adults, more were unable to vote than registered: 60% could not vote versus 40% registered.
accept: Among Nonwhite adults, 60% could not vote, compared with 40% who were registered.
A 60% majority of Nonwhite adults were not registered to vote.
Only 40% of Nonwhite adults were registered; 60% could not vote.
units.evidence: The Nonwhite bar must show a larger 'Couldn't vote' segment at 60% and a smaller 'Registered' segment at 40%.

units.claim: Nonwhite adults were far more likely than White adults to be unable to vote: 60% versus 26%.
accept: Nonwhite adults were more than twice as likely as White adults to be unable to vote: 60% versus 26%.
60% of Nonwhite adults couldn't vote, compared with 26% of White adults.
The couldn't-vote share was 60% for Nonwhite and 26% for White.
Nonwhite non-registration was 34 percentage points higher than White non-registration (60% versus 26%).
units.evidence: Both 'Couldn't vote' segments must be visible/labeled at 60% for Nonwhite and 26% for White, with the Nonwhite segment clearly larger.

optional_valid: White registered share was 1.85 times Nonwhite registered share (74 ÷ 40 = 1.85).
White couldn't-vote share was less than half Nonwhite couldn't-vote share (26% versus 60%).
The registered and couldn't-vote shares are complements within each group: White 74/26, Nonwhite 40/60.

g0_data_completeness.selection: all role=bar data rows; annotation rows excluded
